title: Canonical tool-name registry and staged rename/mapping flow for OpenAI-tool vs legacy-function compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a single canonical registry and migration flow that unifies OpenAI-style 'tool' names and our legacy 'function' identifiers to avoid breaking customer integrations while enabling progressive renames and stricter validation.
recent_activity: 2025-09-08: Ticket created with initial problem statement and scope (Aisha).

2025-09-10: Spike completed to enumerate existing name collisions across hosted catalog (Markus) — found ~42 collisions between tool and function namespaces when case-insensitive normalization applied.
2025-09-12: Design sync with PM (Jorge) and Design (Elena) — decided to separate runtime aliasing from canonical name in control plane.

2025-09-15: Prototype created: control-plane registry service that stores canonical_name, aliases[], source (openai|legacy), deprecation_date, and strict_mode flag. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427 (prototype).
2025-09-18: Engineering review: prefer a staged rename (alias -> redirect -> removal) and an opt-in strict validation mode for customers with test harness to detect breakages before enforcement.
2025-09-20: PM requested addition of telemetry: counts of alias hits, mismatched payload shapes, and number of clients using legacy-only names.
2025-09-22: Added checklist items for rollouts and backwards-compat tests; blocked on console UI for admin rename (ENG-53112).
decision_log: Canonical registry separate from runtime: store mapping in control plane to avoid adding lookup latency to the hot path; runtime caches entries with TTL and watch updates for near-real-time changes.
Aliasing strategy: three-stage lifecycle — 1) alias mapping active (silent mapping), 2) redirect/warning with telemetry and 30-day grace, 3) hard enforcement removal behind strict_mode flag.

Name normalization: normalize on registration only (unicode normalization NFKC), but preserve original string for telemetry; runtime matching is case-insensitive and ignores leading/trailing punctuation when strict_mode=false.

Conflict resolution: if two sources claim the same canonical, leave both as aliases under a single canonical if payload shape is compatible; otherwise require manual developer intervention via console and surface conflict in API errors.

Streaming interactions: tool-name mapping must be applied deterministically at call start. If a mid-stream rename occurs, the runtime continues to emit the original mapped tool id for that request to avoid cross-request drift.

Function vs tool payloads: introduce an adapter layer that validates both shapes. For legacy 'function' JSON-RPC style inputs we convert to tool metadata + structured args before invoking target handler; adapters emit compatibility warnings if shape differs.
Fallback behavior: if no mapping found and legacy name looks like known pattern, runtime will attempt best-effort via heuristics and mark telemetry as 'heuristic_match' for later operator review.
checklist: [ ] Implement control-plane registry service with CRUD and alias lifecycle APIs
[ ] Add runtime cache + watch integration (apply mappings at request start)
[ ] Build adapter for legacy function payloads -> tool metadata conversion
[ ] Add telemetry counters: alias_hits, redirect_warnings, heuristic_matches, payload_shape_mismatches
[ ] Create end-to-end tests: streaming + tool call + mid-rollout rename scenario
[ ] Console UI flow for admin rename and conflict resolution (coordinate with frontend team ENG-53112)
[ ] Run canary with non-critical customers (opt-in) for 4 weeks
[ ] Draft customer migration guide and FAQ
